meta.title: Gillette's Cheap-Razor Trick Wasn't Day-One Genius
meta.hook: Gillette didn't invent cheap razors and pricey blades on day one. Patents forced the wait.
meta.description: King Camp Gillette patented the disposable safety razor blade in 1904 and sold premium-priced razor sets while the patent held. Only after the patent expired in 1921, and rivals could copy the blade, did Gillette introduce a near-cost razor to lock in customers for its blades — the pricing strategy now taught in business schools.

scenes.narration: Everyone credits Gillette for inventing cheap razors and expensive blades. That's not quite how it happened.

scenes.narration: The patent expired in nineteen twenty-one. Competitors could finally copy the blade. That's when the strategy flipped.

scenes.narration: Gillette introduced a one-dollar razor, priced near cost, and let the blades you kept buying carry the margin.
